comments.author: @greyjay9202
comments.text:
When I lived in rural Nevada, in a town of 100 people, I had a friend come to visit me from back East.
On her way, she drove from Elko to Jarbidge in her 1966 Plymouth Valiant.
She said the drive was a bit challenging, but not frightening. Access to Jarbidge
from Idaho is easier. Every state has one or more communities which are
extremely isolated. Mentone, Texas, Grouse Creek, Utah, Estcourt Station, Maine, Supai, Arizona, Midas, Nevada, and Glasgow, Montana come to mind. I would include Clayton Lake, Maine on that list, accessible only by private logging road.

comments.text: We had the privilege to visit Jarbidge this past June. The drive from Idaho was absolutely stunning. Upon arrival, we were immediately welcomed by a wonderful gal who immediately showed us the community hall and gave us camping tips. Lunch at the outdoor Inn was more of the same, good food and warm friendly folks. We shared a beer with a lovely local lady who gave us great history of the area & more tips on camping. Later...this same wonderful person drove her side by side out to the campground to check on us and make sure we had settled in. This is such a rarity these days. This place and these people will be forever impressed upon our hearts. All I can say is the energy of this place is incredibly good! Lastly, the drive south to Elko was even more amazing than the drive in! It took us forever because I kept having to jump out of the truck to simply be dumfounded by the views . We have traveled the west extensively and Jarbidge is by far one of the benchmark experiences of all of our travels.
